records.source: וַיְכֻלּ֛וּ הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ וְכָל־צְבָאָֽם׃
records.gloss: And were finished the heavens and the earth and all their host.
pieces: So the heavens and the earth were completed, with everything in them.

L.1: And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.

R.1: So God finished making the heavens and the earth and everything in them.

decisions.choice: all their host: everything that fills them
decisions.reason: The word means an army, or any great ordered company. Here it gathers up everything that fills the heavens and the earth: the lights and stars of the sky (Deuteronomy 4:19 calls them "the host of heaven") and all that lives on the earth.

decisions.choice: were finished: God finished them
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who finished them, but verse 2 does: God completed his work. The verb means brought to completion, with nothing lacking.

decisions.choice: 2:1-3 closes the account of the seven days
alternatives: the start of a new section with chapter 2
decisions.reason: Chapter divisions were added to the Bible in the Middle Ages. These three verses belong with chapter 1: they close the account of the seven days, and "the heavens and the earth" recalls its first verse. In the Hebrew manuscripts the paragraph break comes after verse 3.

decisions.choice: God finished making
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who finished, as verse 2 does (m2).

records.heading: The seventh day

records.source: וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And completed God on the day the seventh his work which he had done, and he rested on the day the seventh from all his work which he had done.
pieces: On the seventh day God brought to an end the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been doing, and on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done.

L.2: And on the seventh day God completed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested on the seventh day from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done.

R.2: When the seventh day came, God had finished {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work. So on the seventh day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been doing.

decisions.choice: completed on the seventh day: the seventh day is the end of the work, not more work
alternatives: God still did some work on the seventh day
decisions.reason: Read on its own, the first half could suggest that God was still working on the seventh day. The second half says what completing meant: on that day God rested. Finishing the work and ceasing from it are one act, and the seventh day is the completion of the week.

decisions.choice: on the seventh day, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: on the sixth day (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, Syriac)
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint and the Syriac read "on the sixth day", probably so as not to suggest that God worked on the seventh. The Hebrew text, the harder reading, is followed here (m1).

decisions.choice: rested: stopped, ceased from work
decisions.reason: The verb means to stop or cease, and the word Sabbath comes from it. God does not rest because he is tired (Isaiah 40:28); he stops because the work is complete. Exodus 20:11 and 31:17 make this the pattern for Israel's Sabbath.

decisions.choice: work: a task, especially skilled work
decisions.reason: The word is used for skilled work such as the making of the tabernacle (Exodus 36:1-2), and for the work that is not to be done on the Sabbath (Exodus 20:9-10).

decisions.choice: brought to an end ... stopped
decisions.reason: Balanced says "brought to an end" and "stopped" so that the sentence does not seem to say that God worked on the seventh day (m1, m3). Literal keeps "completed" and "rested", and Readable says "had finished" and "rested".

records.source: וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־י֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכָּל־מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: And blessed God the day the seventh and made holy it, because on it he rested from all his work which created God to make.
pieces: God blessed the seventh day and set it apart as holy, since on that day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, all that God had created and made.

L.3: And God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work that God had created to make.

R.3: God blessed the seventh day and made it a holy day. On that day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rested from all the work {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done in creating the world.

decisions.choice: made holy: set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: To make something holy is to set it apart for God. The first thing in the Bible that God makes holy is a day, not a place or an object. Israel is later told to keep the Sabbath holy for this reason (Exodus 20:8-11).

decisions.choice: which God created to make: all the work God did in creating
alternatives: which God created so that it would go on making
decisions.reason: The words "created" and "to make" are joined to sum up the whole of God's work. The phrase closes the account with both of its main verbs: "create" (verses 1, 21, 27) and "make" (verses 7, 16, 25, 31).

decisions.choice: the seventh day has no evening and morning
decisions.reason: Each of the six days ends with "there was evening and there was morning". The seventh does not: the account ends with the day God blessed and made holy. Hebrews 4:3-10 draws on this to speak of God's rest as still open to his people.

decisions.choice: that God had created to make
alternatives: that God had created and made
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "created to make" (m2); Balanced says "created and made".

decisions.choice: set it apart as holy
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "set apart" to say what "holy" means (m1).

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה תוֹלְד֧וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ בְּהִבָּֽרְאָ֑ם בְּי֗וֹם עֲשׂ֛וֹת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶ֥רֶץ וְשָׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: These [are the] generations of the heavens and the earth in their being created, in [the] day of making [by] YHWH God earth and heavens.
pieces: This is the story of the heavens and the earth as they were created. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made earth and heavens,

L.4: These [are] the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made earth and heavens.

R.4: This is the story of how the heavens and the earth came to be. It begins at the time when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made the earth and the sky.

decisions.choice: generations: an account of what came from them
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to father, to give birth" and usually introduces a family line (5:1; 10:1). Genesis uses "these are the generations of ..." ten times to open a new section, which tells what came from the one named rather than how it began. Here it introduces what came from the heavens and the earth: the story of the man and the woman that follows.

decisions.choice: the first half heads the new account; the second half begins its first sentence
alternatives: the first half closes the account of the seven days (1:1-2:3)
decisions.reason: Everywhere else in Genesis "these are the generations of" opens a section, so the first half of the verse most likely heads the story that follows. Many readers take it instead as the close of 1:1-2:3, since "the heavens and the earth" and "created" echo 1:1. The two halves mirror each other: "the heavens and the earth ... created", then "earth and heavens ... made". The second half begins a sentence that runs to verse 7.

decisions.choice: the LORD: YHWH, the personal name of God
decisions.reason: Here, for the first time, God is called by his own name, written with four consonants, YHWH. Exodus 3:14-15 links it with the verb "to be". In time Jewish readers stopped saying the name aloud out of reverence and read "Lord" in its place; the Hebrew manuscripts carry the vowels of that word, and the Septuagint translates the name "Lord". How the name was first pronounced is not recorded; Yahweh is the form most scholars reconstruct.

decisions.choice: the LORD God: the name joined with the title God
decisions.reason: Chapters 2 and 3 join the name and "God" again and again, a pairing that is rare elsewhere. It tells the reader that the God of chapter 1, maker of everything, is the LORD, the God who later makes himself known to Israel by name (Exodus 6:2-3), and who here deals closely with the man and the woman.

decisions.choice: the LORD (default); Yahweh (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: Following long custom, the name is written "the LORD" in capital letters, to set it apart from the title "Lord" (m3). The divine name setting shows "Yahweh" instead. "Jehovah", an older form, combines the consonants of the name with the vowels of the word for Lord.

decisions.choice: the story of
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "generations". Balanced and Readable say "story", since here the word introduces an account of what followed (m1).

records.heading: The man and the woman in the garden of Eden

records.source: וְכֹ֣ל׀שִׂ֣יחַ הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה טֶ֚רֶם יִֽהְיֶ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ וְכָל־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה טֶ֣רֶם יִצְמָ֑ח כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הִמְטִ֜יר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאָדָ֣ם אַ֔יִן לַֽעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And every shrub of the field not yet was in the earth, and every plant of the field not yet sprouted, for not had caused rain YHWH God on the earth, and [a] human there was not to work the ground,
pieces: no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no one to work the ground.

L.5: and no shrub of the field was yet in the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprouted, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no human to work the ground,

R.5: There were no bushes or crops growing in the fields yet. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God had not sent any rain on the earth, and there was no one to farm the land.

decisions.choice: shrub of the field, plant of the field: wild bushes, and crops that need someone to grow them
decisions.reason: The account names two kinds of growth that are missing: wild shrubs, which need rain, and the plants of the field, the crops people grow (3:18 uses the same words for the food the man will grow). Each lack is matched by its cause: no rain, and no one to work the ground. The verse does not speak of all plant life, and so does not contradict 1:11-12; it describes a land not yet farmed.

decisions.choice: a human to work the ground: adam and adamah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on the human (adam) and the ground (adamah): the land waits for someone to work it, and in verse 7 the human is formed from it. The verb "work" is used again in 2:15 and 3:23; it also means "serve".

decisions.choice: no shrub ... yet
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "every shrub ... not yet was"; English says "no shrub ... yet".

records.source: וְאֵ֖ד יַֽעֲלֶ֣ה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִשְׁקָ֖ה אֶֽת־כָּל־פְּנֵֽי־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: and a stream went up from the earth and watered all [the] face of the ground.
pieces: Instead, water would well up from the earth and soak the whole surface of the ground.

L.6: and a stream would go up from the earth and water the whole face of the ground.

R.6: But water came up out of the ground and watered all the land.

decisions.choice: a flow of water rising from the earth
decisions.reason: The word is rare; it is used again only in Job 36:27, where it is linked with rain. Older translations said "mist". A similar word in Akkadian means the flood of a river, and rising "from the earth" suits water welling up from below, like the deep waters of 7:11 and 49:25. Either way, the ground is watered before anyone works it.

decisions.choice: would go up, would water: something that happened again and again
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a repeated or ongoing action in the past, setting the scene for verse 7.

records.source: וַיִּיצֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֗ם עָפָר֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וַיִּפַּ֥ח בְּאַפָּ֖יו נִשְׁמַ֣ת חַיִּ֑ים וַֽיְהִ֥י הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְנֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And formed YHWH God the man, dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils breath of life, and became the man a living creature.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God shaped the man out of dust from the ground. He breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God formed the man, dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature.

R.7: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made a man out of dust from the ground, like a potter shaping clay. He breathed the breath of life into the man's nose, and the man came to life.

decisions.choice: formed: shaped, as a potter shapes clay
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a potter at work (Jeremiah 18:2-6; Isaiah 64:8). Chapter 1 tells of God's word; this account shows his hands, shaping the man as a potter shapes a pot.

decisions.choice: the man: the first human, formed from the ground
alternatives: the human, not yet male or female
decisions.reason: He is called "the human" (ha-adam), a play on "the ground" (ha-adamah) that he is formed from. With the article the word is not yet a personal name. The story treats him as one person, and when the woman is made from him he calls himself "man" (ish, verse 23).

decisions.choice: the breath of life: life given by God's own breath
decisions.reason: The man's life comes from God's breath, given to no other creature in the account. The phrase returns in 7:22. "Living creature" is the phrase used of the animals in 1:20-24: the man is alive as they are, but he received his life directly from God.

decisions.choice: shaped
decisions.reason: Balanced says "shaped" to keep the picture of the potter (m1).

decisions.choice: like a potter shaping clay
decisions.reason: Readable adds the picture of the potter to show what "formed" means (m1).

records.source: וַיִּטַּ֞ע יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים גַּן־בְעֵ֖דֶן מִקֶּ֑דֶם וַיָּ֣שֶׂם שָׁ֔ם אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצָֽר׃
records.gloss: And planted YHWH God a garden in Eden from [the] east, and put there the man whom he had formed.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} placed the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had shaped.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put there the man whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had formed.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God planted a garden in a place called Eden, in the east. He put the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made there.

decisions.choice: Eden: a region, with the garden in it
decisions.reason: Eden sounds like a Hebrew word for delight or plenty. The garden is planted in Eden and is not the same as Eden: a river flows out of Eden to water the garden (verse 10).

decisions.choice: in the east: toward the east
alternatives: in ancient times, at the beginning
decisions.reason: The word can mean the east or long ago (Psalm 74:12). Here it places the garden toward the east, as later the way back to it lies to the east (3:24; 4:16).

records.source: וַיַּצְמַ֞ח יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כָּל־עֵ֛ץ נֶחְמָ֥ד לְמַרְאֶ֖ה וְט֣וֹב לְמַאֲכָ֑ל וְעֵ֤ץ הַֽחַיִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַגָּ֔ן וְעֵ֕ץ הַדַּ֖עַת ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע׃
records.gloss: And made sprout YHWH God from the ground every tree desirable to sight and good for food, and [the] tree of the life in [the] middle of the garden, and [the] tree of the knowledge [of] good and evil.
pieces: Out of the ground {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made every tree grow that is pleasing to look at and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made to sprout from the ground every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food, and the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground. They were beautiful to look at, and their fruit was good to eat. In the middle of the garden was the tree that gives life. There was also the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil.

decisions.choice: the tree of life: a tree whose fruit gives life
decisions.reason: In 3:22 eating from it would let a person live for ever. Proverbs uses the picture for wisdom (Proverbs 3:18), and Revelation 22:2 shows the tree again in the new creation.

decisions.choice: the knowledge of good and evil: deciding for oneself what is good and what is bad
decisions.reason: The phrase can name the ability to judge between good and bad, as a king must (1 Kings 3:9), or that a grown person has and a small child does not (Deuteronomy 1:39). Pairs of opposites can also mean "everything". The story does not define it, but 3:5 and 3:22 show it as something that belongs to God, which human beings take for themselves.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the garden: said of the tree of life, and perhaps of both trees
alternatives: only the tree of life was in the middle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew places the tree of life in the middle of the garden and then adds the tree of knowledge, so it is not clear whether both stood there. In 3:3 the woman speaks of "the tree in the middle of the garden" and means the tree of knowledge, so both may have been there.

decisions.choice: the tree that gives life; the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil
alternatives: the tree of life; the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
decisions.reason: Readable says what each tree does (m1, m2), since "tree of life" alone can sound like a name with no meaning.

records.source: וְנָהָרּ֙יֹצֵ֣א מֵעֵ֔דֶן לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת אֶת־הַגָּ֑ן וּמִשָּׁם֙ יִפָּרֵ֔ד וְהָיָ֖ה לְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה רָאשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And a river [was] going out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads.
pieces: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it split into four branches.

L.10: And a river was going out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads.

R.10: A river flowed out of Eden and watered the garden. After that it split into four rivers.

decisions.choice: heads: branches
decisions.reason: The word means "heads". A river's heads can be its sources or the points where it divides. Flowing out from the garden, this river divides into four branches that run out into the known world (verses 11-14).

decisions.choice: a river flowing out to give water: a picture taken up by later scripture
decisions.reason: Later scripture speaks of a river that flows out from where God is and gives life: Psalm 46:5, Ezekiel 47:1-12 and Revelation 22:1-2.

records.source: שֵׁ֥ם הָֽאֶחָ֖ד פִּישׁ֑וֹן ה֣וּא הַסֹּבֵ֗ב אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽחֲוִילָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃
records.gloss: [The] name of the one [is] Pishon; it [is] the [one] going around all [the] land of the Havilah, where there [is] the gold.
pieces: The first is named Pishon. It winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

L.11: The name of the first [is] Pishon; it [is] the one that goes around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

R.11: The first river is called the Pishon. It flows around the whole land of Havilah, where gold is found.

decisions.choice: Pishon and Havilah: a river and a land not known today
decisions.reason: The Pishon is not named anywhere else, and where it ran is unknown. Havilah appears among the peoples of Arabia (10:29; 25:18), so the river may have been thought of as lying to the south or east. The writer describes it for readers who knew it, by the gold that made the land famous.

decisions.choice: the first
decisions.reason: Hebrew counts with "one" where English says "first" (as in 1:5).

records.source: וּֽזֲהַ֛ב הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִ֖וא ט֑וֹב שָׁ֥ם הַבְּדֹ֖לַח וְאֶ֥בֶן הַשֹּֽׁהַם׃
records.gloss: And [the] gold of the land the that [is] good; there [is] the bdellium and the stone of the onyx.
pieces: The gold of that land is good, and aromatic resin and onyx stone are found there as well.

L.12: And the gold of that land [is] good; bdellium [is] there, and the onyx stone.

R.12: The gold of that land is of fine quality. Sweet-smelling resin and precious onyx stones are also found there.

decisions.choice: bdellium: a fragrant resin, or perhaps a pearl
decisions.reason: The word appears again only in Numbers 11:7, where manna looks like it. It is usually taken to be a sweet-smelling gum from a tree, valued in the ancient world; some have taken it to be a pearl.

decisions.choice: onyx: a precious stone, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: Onyx stones were set on the high priest's garments (Exodus 28:9-12, 20). The exact stone is not known. Gold and precious stones later adorn the tabernacle, one of several links between the garden and the place where God lives among his people.

decisions.choice: aromatic resin (B); sweet-smelling resin (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bdellium", the traditional word; Balanced and Readable say what it most likely was (m1).

records.source: וְשֵֽׁם־הַנָּהָ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י גִּיח֑וֹן ה֣וּא הַסּוֹבֵ֔ב אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ כּֽוּשׁ׃
records.gloss: And [the] name of the river the second [is] Gihon; it [is] the [one] going around all [the] land of Cush.
pieces: The second river is named Gihon. It winds through the whole land of Cush.

L.13: And the name of the second river [is] Gihon; it [is] the one that goes around the whole land of Cush.

R.13: The second river is called the Gihon. It flows around the whole land of Cush.

decisions.choice: Gihon and Cush: probably a land to the east here, though Cush usually means the land south of Egypt
alternatives: Cush as Ethiopia, with the Gihon as the Nile
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Cush usually names the land south of Egypt, roughly today's Sudan (Isaiah 18:1). But 10:8 links Cush with Nimrod, whose kingdom was in Mesopotamia, and the name here may point east, near the Tigris and Euphrates. Gihon is also the name of the spring of Jerusalem (1 Kings 1:33).

records.source: וְשֵׁ֨ם הַנָּהָ֤ר הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ חִדֶּ֔קֶל ה֥וּא הַֽהֹלֵ֖ךְ קִדְמַ֣ת אַשּׁ֑וּר וְהַנָּהָ֥ר הָֽרְבִיעִ֖י ה֥וּא פְרָֽת׃
records.gloss: And [the] name of the river the third [is] Tigris; it [is] the [one] going east of Assyria. And the river the fourth, it [is] Euphrates.
pieces: The third river is named Tigris. It runs east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

L.14: And the name of the third river [is] Tigris; it [is] the one that goes east of Assyria. And the fourth river, it [is the] Euphrates.

R.14: The third river is called the Tigris. It flows along the east side of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.

decisions.choice: Tigris and Euphrates: the two great rivers of Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name of the third river, Hiddeqel, is the Tigris (Daniel 10:4). With the Euphrates, which needs no description, it places the garden in or near Mesopotamia, the land between these two rivers. The four rivers together reach to the edges of the world the first readers knew.

decisions.choice: east of Assyria
decisions.reason: The word can mean "east of" or "in front of". The Tigris runs through the heart of Assyria, and the phrase may describe it as seen from the writer's own land.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֛ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּנִּחֵ֣הוּ בְגַן־עֵ֔דֶן לְעָבְדָ֖הּ וּלְשָׁמְרָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And took YHWH God the man and put him in [the] garden of Eden to work it and to keep it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.

L.15: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God took the man and placed him in the garden of Eden to work it and to keep it.

R.15: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God put the man in the garden of Eden to farm it and take care of it.

decisions.choice: placed: settled, gave a place of rest
decisions.reason: The verb is not the one used for "put" in verse 8. It comes from the word for rest, and is used for God giving his people rest in their land (Deuteronomy 3:20) and for setting something before the LORD (Exodus 16:33-34).

decisions.choice: to work it and keep it: to tend the garden and to guard it
alternatives: to farm it and protect it, with no wider sense
decisions.reason: The first verb means to work or to serve; the second means to keep, watch over or guard. The same two verbs describe the work of the Levites at the tabernacle (Numbers 3:7-8), so the garden is pictured as a holy place and the man as its keeper. Work belongs to the good world from the start; it is not a result of the curse in 3:17-19. The word "it" is feminine in Hebrew, though "garden" is masculine, and may point back to "the ground" (verse 5).

decisions.choice: settled him
decisions.reason: Balanced says "settled" to keep the sense of rest in the verb (m1).

records.source: וַיְצַו֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל־הָֽאָדָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר מִכֹּ֥ל עֵֽץ־הַגָּ֖ן אָכֹ֥ל תֹּאכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And commanded YHWH God on the man, saying, from every tree of the garden eating you will eat,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God commanded the man, "You may eat as much as you like from any tree in the garden,

L.16: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God commanded the man, saying, "From every tree of the garden you may surely eat,

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God gave the man a command. He said, "You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,

decisions.choice: you may surely eat: the doubled verb makes the permission generous
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb ("eating you will eat") for emphasis. In a permission it stresses freedom: the man may eat from every tree, with one exception. The same doubling marks the warning of verse 17, "you will surely die".

decisions.choice: commanded the man: the command is given before the woman is made
decisions.reason: God gives the command to the man alone. In 3:2-3 the woman knows it, so the story assumes it was passed on to her.

records.source: וּמֵעֵ֗ץ הַדַּ֨עַת֙ ט֣וֹב וָרָ֔ע לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם אֲכָלְךָ֥ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מ֥וֹת תָּמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: but from [the] tree of the knowledge [of] good and evil not you will eat from it, for in [the] day of your eating from it dying you will die.
pieces: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, because on the day you eat from it, you will surely die."

L.17: but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat from it you will surely die."

R.17: but do not eat from the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil. If you eat its fruit, you will certainly die."

decisions.choice: you shall not eat: a lasting prohibition
decisions.reason: "Not" with this verb form is the strong, lasting kind of command used in the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:13-15).

decisions.choice: on the day you eat from it you will surely die: from that day death is certain
alternatives: you will die before that day ends
you will die inwardly that day
decisions.reason: "In the day" often means simply "when" (2:4). The doubled verb, "dying you will die", is the form of a death sentence (1 Kings 2:37, 42; Ezekiel 3:18). When the man and the woman eat, they do not die that day, but they are sent away from the tree of life (3:22-24), and death becomes certain for them (3:19). Some readers also see a death on that day in their broken relationship with God.

decisions.choice: If you eat its fruit
alternatives: on the day you eat from it
decisions.reason: Readable says "if" for "in the day", which here means "when" (m2), so that young readers do not take it to mean the same day.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹא־ט֛וֹב הֱי֥וֹת הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְבַדּ֑וֹ אֶֽעֱשֶׂהּ־לּ֥וֹעֵ֖זֶר כְּנֶגְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH God, not good [is] the being of the man by himself; I will make for him a helper as opposite him.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said, "It is not good for the man to be on his own. I will make him a helper who matches him."

L.18: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said, "It is not good [for] the man to be alone; I will make for him a helper corresponding to him."

R.18: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a partner who is just right for him."

decisions.choice: not good: the first thing in creation called not good
decisions.reason: Throughout chapter 1 God saw that what he made was good. Here, for the first time, something is not good: the man alone. Human beings are made for companionship.

decisions.choice: helper: one who gives help the other needs, not a lesser assistant
decisions.reason: The word does not suggest a lower rank: it is most often used of God himself as the helper of his people (Exodus 18:4; Psalm 33:20; 121:1-2). It names someone who gives help that is needed.

decisions.choice: corresponding to him: like him and facing him, his counterpart
decisions.reason: The phrase joins "like" and "in front of, opposite". The helper will be his equal and his match, someone who stands face to face with him, as no animal can (verse 20).

decisions.choice: partner
decisions.reason: In plain English "helper" can suggest a lesser assistant, which the Hebrew does not mean (m2), so Readable says "partner".

decisions.choice: who matches him
decisions.reason: Balanced says "matches" to keep both sides of the phrase, likeness and facing (m3).

records.source: וַיִּצֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה כָּל־חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיָּבֵא֙ אֶל־הָ֣אָדָ֔ם לִרְא֖וֹת מַה־יִּקְרָא־ל֑וֹ וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקְרָא־ל֧וֹ הָֽאָדָ֛ם נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה ה֥וּא שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And formed YHWH God from the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and brought [them] to the man to see what he would call it; and all that called it the man, living creature, that [was] its name.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God formed out of the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would name them. Whatever the man called each living creature, that became its name.

L.19: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God formed from the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought [them] to the man to see what he would call each one; and whatever the man called each living creature, that [was] its name.

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God made all the wild animals and all the birds out of the ground. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them to the man to see what names he would give them. Whatever the man called each living thing, that was its name.

decisions.choice: formed: told here in the order of this story, not as a new order of creation
alternatives: had formed (before the man was made)
decisions.reason: The verb form usually tells the next event, which would put the making of the animals after the man, unlike chapter 1. It can also look back ("had formed"). Either way, this account is told around the man and his need: the animals are brought to him as possible companions, and its order is the order of the story.

decisions.choice: to see what he would call them: the man names the animals
decisions.reason: In chapter 1 God names day, night, sky, land and seas (1:5, 8, 10). Here he lets the man name the animals, a sign of the rule given to human beings in 1:26-28, and waits "to see" what he will do.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם שֵׁמ֗וֹת לְכָל־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּלְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּלְאָדָ֕ם לֹֽא־מָצָ֥א עֵ֖זֶר כְּנֶגְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And called the man names to all the livestock and to [the] bird[s] of the heavens and to every animal of the field, but for [the] man not he found a helper as opposite him.
pieces: The man gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the sky and every wild animal. But no helper who matched him was found for the man.

L.20: And the man gave names to all the livestock and to the birds of the heavens and to every animal of the field, but for the man he did not find a helper corresponding to him.

R.20: So the man gave names to all the farm animals, the birds and the wild animals. But none of them was the right partner for the man.

decisions.choice: for the man: not yet the name Adam
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew vowels give the word without the article, so it can be read as the name Adam, and some translations begin to use the name here. But the story goes on to speak of "the man" in the next verses, and the name is plainly used only from 4:25, so it is taken as "the man".

decisions.choice: he did not find: the one who looks is not named
decisions.reason: The verb is "he found", with no subject named. It may be the man, who finds no partner among the animals, or God.

decisions.choice: was found
decisions.reason: Balanced leaves the finder unnamed, as the Hebrew does (m2), by saying "was found".

records.source: וַיַּפֵּל֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀תַּרְדֵּמָ֛ה עַל־הָאָדָ֖ם וַיִּישָׁ֑ן וַיִּקַּ֗ח אַחַת֙ מִצַּלְעֹתָ֔יו וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר בָּשָׂ֖ר תַּחְתֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And caused to fall YHWH God a deep sleep on the man, and he slept; and he took one from his sides, and closed flesh in its place.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made the man fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God caused a deep sleep to fall on the man, and he slept; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took one of his sides and closed up [the] flesh in its place.

R.21: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made the man fall into a deep sleep. While he was sleeping, God took out one of his ribs. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} closed up the place with flesh.

decisions.choice: deep sleep: a heavy sleep sent by God
decisions.reason: The word is used of a sleep that God sends, sometimes with a vision (15:12; 1 Samuel 26:12). The man does not see what God does.

decisions.choice: one of his sides: a rib, or one side of him
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the word means the side of something: of the ark of the covenant or of a hill (Exodus 25:12; 2 Samuel 16:13), and the side rooms of the temple (1 Kings 6:5). Here it may be a rib, or a whole side of the man. Either way, the woman is made from the man's own body, "bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh" (verse 23).

decisions.choice: sides (L); ribs (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "side", the word's usual sense; Balanced and Readable say "rib", the traditional reading and the likelier one here (m2). The same applies in verse 22.

records.source: וַיִּבֶן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀אֶֽת־הַצֵּלָ֛ע אֲשֶׁר־לָקַ֥ח מִן־הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיְבִאֶ֖הָ אֶל־הָֽאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And built YHWH God the side which he had taken from the man into a woman, and brought her to the man.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God built a woman out of the rib {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken from the man, and brought her to him.

L.22: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God built the side that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken from the man into a woman, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought her to the man.

R.22: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made a woman from the rib {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken out of the man. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought her to the man.

decisions.choice: built: God builds the woman, as one builds a house
decisions.reason: The man was formed like a pot (verse 7); the woman is built, the verb used for a house or a city. The account gives the making of the woman its own careful description.

decisions.choice: brought her to the man: God presents the woman, as a bride is brought to her husband
decisions.reason: God brings the woman to the man as he brought the animals (verse 19), and as a bride was brought to her husband. This time the man answers with joy (verse 23).

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ הָֽאָדָם֒ זֹ֣את הַפַּ֗עַם עֶ֚צֶם מֵֽעֲצָמַ֔י וּבָשָׂ֖ר מִבְּשָׂרִ֑י לְזֹאת֙ יִקָּרֵ֣א אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּ֥י מֵאִ֖ישׁ לֻֽקֳחָה־זֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And said the man, this one, this time, [is] bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh; to this one will be called woman, because from man was taken this one.
pieces: The man said, "At last, here is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh! She will be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man."

L.23: And the man said, "This one at last [is] bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; this one shall be called Woman, because from Man this one was taken."

R.23: Then the man said, "At last! Here is someone like me, made from my own bones and my own body! She will be called 'woman,' because she was taken out of a man."

decisions.choice: bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh: my own kin, one with me
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for close family (29:14; 2 Samuel 5:1). The man knows the woman as one of his own kind, the partner he did not find among the animals.

decisions.choice: woman (ishah) ... man (ish): two words that sound alike
decisions.reason: The man's words play on two Hebrew words that sound alike, ish (man) and ishah (woman), though they come from different roots. Here the word for the man changes from "the human" (adam) to "man" (ish), the word for a male, now that there is a woman.

decisions.choice: this one ... this one ... this one: the first human words are a poem of delight
decisions.reason: The man says "this one" three times: at the start, in the middle and at the end. His words, the first a human being speaks in the Bible, are a short poem, and "this time" (at last) sets the woman apart from the animals that came before.

decisions.choice: Woman ... Man (capitals)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced capitalise the words to show that they are names given (m2); Readable puts "woman" in quotation marks.

decisions.choice: someone like me, made from my own bones and my own body
alternatives: bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1) and keeps its picture of bone and body.

records.source: עַל־כֵּן֙ יַֽעֲזָב־אִ֔ישׁ אֶת־אָבִ֖יו וְאֶת־אִמּ֑וֹ וְדָבַ֣ק בְּאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְהָי֖וּ לְבָשָׂ֥ר אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: Therefore leaves a man his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become flesh one.
pieces: This is why a man leaves his father and mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.

L.24: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.

R.24: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and they become one, like one body.

decisions.choice: therefore: the narrator draws a lesson from the story
decisions.reason: These are most likely the narrator's words, not the man's: from the story they draw a truth for every marriage. The woman made from the man's body and brought to him is the reason a man and his wife become one. Jesus quotes the verse as God's own word (Matthew 19:4-6; Mark 10:6-9).

decisions.choice: clings: holds fast, in faithful loyalty
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick to something, and is also used for Israel's loyalty to the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:20; 30:20). It speaks of lasting commitment.

decisions.choice: one flesh: one family and one life, including the bodily union of marriage
decisions.reason: "Flesh" can mean a body, a person, or a family (29:14). The phrase includes sexual union but is wider: husband and wife become one new family, closer than their ties to the parents they leave.

decisions.choice: and they become one flesh, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: and the two become one flesh (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read "and the two become one flesh", the form in which the New Testament quotes it (Matthew 19:5; 1 Corinthians 6:16; Ephesians 5:31). The Hebrew text has "they"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: they become one, like one body
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m3), keeping its picture of the body.

records.source: וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ שְׁנֵיהֶם֙ עֲרוּמִּ֔ים הָֽאָדָ֖ם וְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֖א יִתְבֹּשָֽׁשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: And they were, [the] two of them, naked, the man and his wife, and not they were ashamed.
pieces: Both of them, the man and his wife, were naked, yet they were not ashamed.

L.25: And the two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

R.25: The man and his wife did not wear any clothes, but they did not feel ashamed.

decisions.choice: naked: without clothing, open and unprotected
decisions.reason: The word sounds like "crafty", the word that describes the serpent in the next verse (3:1), a play that links the two scenes. Here nakedness is innocence: they have nothing to hide from each other or from God, until 3:7-10.

decisions.choice: they were not ashamed: they felt no shame before each other
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a lasting state. Shame comes with the first disobedience, when they see that they are naked and cover themselves (3:7).
